name: Google
label: works on my machine, until user 101
summary: Sign in with Google is easy. The moment you ask for Gmail, Drive or Calendar, you're in a verification queue, and for the restricted ones, a paid security assessment.
blocker: Sensitive or restricted scopes mean verification, and past 100 new users unverified you are locked out for the project's lifetime.

steps.title: Open the Google Auth Platform in a Cloud project
steps.detail: Google's console splits this into: get started, audience, branding, clients and data access. We could read the section names, not a click-by-click.

steps.title: Pick the audience
steps.detail: External means any Google account. Internal means members of your Cloud organization only, and everyone else gets org_internal. Start External in Testing.

steps.title: Branding: name, logo, privacy policy, homepage
steps.detail: A privacy policy URL is required for verification. The domain has to be verified in Search Console by a Project Owner or Editor who is also a verified property owner.

steps.title: Declare data access (scopes)
steps.detail: This choice sets your whole timeline. Sign-in scopes are free. Sensitive scopes need verification. Restricted scopes need verification plus a security assessment.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client and add redirect URIs
steps.detail: Web application client with your callback. Changing redirect URIs or origins after verification triggers re-verification, so settle them first.

steps.title: Test with up to 100 test users
steps.detail: In Testing, only listed users can authorize, and their authorizations (refresh tokens included) expire after 7 days.

steps.title: Publish and submit for verification
steps.detail: Publish the app, then submit: privacy policy, domain proof, and per-scope justification with a demo video showing each scope in use. Until approved, users see the unverified-app screen.

steps.title: Restricted scopes only: pass the security assessment
steps.detail: Gmail-class scopes need an independent assessment (CASA) and a Letter of Validation, renewed every 12 months. A vendor article puts weeks to months on it.

nuances.text: If you only ask for openid, email and profile, or use Sign in with Google, you skip the test-user list, the warning screen and the 7-day expiry.
nuances.note: The most useful sentence in Google's docs for most apps.

nuances.text: Unverified apps are capped at 100 new users in total after the warning screen appears. The cap lasts for the life of the project and can't be reset.
Re-verification is needed when you add redirect URLs or JavaScript origins, rename the product, or change clients or scopes after approval.
Internal-only apps, apps still in development or testing, and OAuth-based plugins don't need verification.
Restricted-scope apps repeat the security assessment every 12 months, counted from the previous Letter of Validation.
Google references a $15,000 to $75,000 range for the security assessment.
nuances.note: Secondhand, from a vendor who sells assessments, in a 2021 article. Confirm the current price with an assessor.
Not on any Google page we could open. Every timeline above is from the vendor article.

blockers.symptom: Users get signed out after a week
blockers.cause: The app is in Testing, where authorizations expire 7 days after consent.
blockers.fix: Publish to production, or limit scopes to sign-in.

blockers.symptom: Unverified app warning on the consent screen
blockers.cause: Sensitive or restricted scopes without verification, or scopes in code that differ from the consent screen.
blockers.fix: Make code and consent screen match, then submit for verification.

blockers.symptom: Verification keeps coming back with questions
blockers.cause: Each scope has to be justified in writing and shown in a demo video. Vague submissions get clarification rounds.
blockers.fix: One justification and one video segment per scope.

blockers.cause: Audience is Internal and the user is outside your Cloud organization.

agent: Pick the smallest scope set and say which tier each lands in
Write the privacy policy page from your actual data flows
Write the demo video script, scope by scope
you: Create the project and verify the domain in Search Console
Buy the security assessment if you touch restricted scopes

redirect.rule: Register each redirect URI on the OAuth client. Adding one after verification triggers re-verification.
